subject: english-literature
title: Formalism and Marxism
welcome_lead: Two opposing lenses: one polishes the text in isolation, the other reads it as ideology's child.
meta_desc: Formalism and Marxist criticism at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have set form against ideology — and seen that the best readings often borrow from both.

walkthroughs.body_html:
New Critics insisted on the autonomy of the text. Wimsatt and Beardsley's intentional fallacy (1946) bars author biography; the affective fallacy bars reader response.

What remains is the verbal artefact, prized for ambiguity, paradox and irony.
Russian Formalist Viktor Shklovsky argued art's purpose is ostranenie: making the stone stony again, refreshing perception dulled by habit.

Marxist criticism reads texts as both reflections and producers of ideology. Eagleton's Literary Theory (1983) is the great introduction.

A novel of bourgeois marriage reproduces a bourgeois ideology of selfhood — or, occasionally, ruptures it.

mcqs.q: Wimsatt and Beardsley's 'intentional fallacy' was formulated in:

options: Defamiliarisation
Imitation
Catharsis
Hubris
Experimentation with form (fragmentation, stream of consciousness), focus on subjective interior experience, scepticism toward traditional narrative and absolute truth.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Modernism just means literature written in modern times.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
Pathetic fallacy is when an argument in a story is weak or sad.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
Attributing human emotions or qualities to nature or inanimate objects to reflect a character's feelings or scene's mood (e.g. angry storms during conflict).
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.

mcqs.q: What is the function of dystopian fiction?
options: Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
Dystopian fiction is just storytelling set in scary futures.
To critique tendencies in the writer's own society by extrapolating them into a nightmarish future — dystopias hold up a warning mirror to the present.
